chunks: And as for what Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from al-'Ala' ibn Muhammad from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washsha' from Abd Allah ibn Sinan, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Nursing does not make forbidden (in marriage) except that which causes the flesh to grow and the bone to strengthen.'
ai.seo_question: What is the criterion for nursing to establish marital prohibition in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Ishtibār clarifies the juristic criterion for *radāʿ* (nursing kinship), specifying that only nursing substantial enough to nourish the body—causing flesh to grow and bones to strengthen—creates a permanent marital prohibition. This distinction excludes mere sucking or minimal intake, a view widely accepted in Shia fiqh to prevent excessive expansion of the mahram circle. The narration underscores the practical application of Quranic principles by linking physical development to legal status.
